transcript.speaker: Jordan Blake
transcript.text: Okay, thanks everyone for joining, this is our final readiness review before Data Driven Or Die launches October first, so I want to make sure we're all aligned before we hit go.

transcript.speaker: Nina Patel
transcript.text: Sounds good, I've got the full plan pulled up, happy to walk through it section by section.

transcript.speaker: Maya Chen
transcript.text: Works for me, and I want to make sure we land on the landing page copy review before we leave, that's been on my list.

transcript.speaker: Sam Whitfield
transcript.text: Same, mostly here to make sure sales is set up to actually work the leads this thing generates, last campaign we dropped the ball on follow up timing.

transcript.speaker: Jordan Blake
transcript.text: Fair, we'll get to that. Nina, can you start with where budget and channel allocation landed?

transcript.speaker: Nina Patel
transcript.text: Sure. Total budget is forty five thousand, we've got twenty thousand going to paid social, mostly LinkedIn given our buyer profile, fifteen thousand across four industry newsletters, and ten thousand for the three part webinar series including production costs.

transcript.speaker: Maya Chen
transcript.text: How'd we land on that split versus last quarter?

transcript.speaker: Nina Patel
transcript.text: We shifted about five thousand out of newsletters and into paid social, the newsletter performance last campaign underdelivered on cost per lead, it came in around ninety dollars a lead versus forty two for paid social.

transcript.speaker: Jordan Blake
transcript.text: Right, and that ninety dollar number is why we trimmed two of the six newsletters we were considering this time and kept only the four that actually converted last time.

transcript.speaker: Sam Whitfield
transcript.text: Makes sense, more efficient spend is good for me either way, as long as lead quality holds.

transcript.speaker: Nina Patel
transcript.text: On quality, we've tightened our MQL criteria too, this campaign specifically targets director level and above at companies with two hundred plus employees, since that's where our sales cycle actually closes fastest.

transcript.speaker: Sam Whitfield
transcript.text: Good, that filtering matters a lot, last time we got a bunch of leads from smaller companies that never had budget authority and it wasted a ton of my team's time.

transcript.speaker: Jordan Blake
transcript.text: Agreed, that's a direct fix based on your feedback from last quarter, appreciate you flagging it then.

transcript.speaker: Sam Whitfield
transcript.text: Of course, that's what the debrief's for.

transcript.speaker: Jordan Blake
transcript.text: Let's talk creative. Nina, walk through the testing results.

transcript.speaker: Nina Patel
transcript.text: We ran an A/B test on the primary ad creative, one version led with feature messaging, dashboards, integrations, that kind of thing, the other led with a customer testimonial from Northstar Logistics talking about time saved on reporting.

transcript.speaker: Maya Chen
transcript.text: And the testimonial version won, right? I remember hearing that at product sync.

transcript.speaker: Nina Patel
transcript.text: Yeah, by a wide margin actually, almost double the click through rate, two point one percent versus one point one for the feature-led version. We're going with testimonial-led creative across all paid social.

transcript.speaker: Jordan Blake
transcript.text: We also got a second testimonial in from a company called Fenwick Manufacturing that we're going to rotate in as a second variant once the campaign's been live a couple weeks, just to avoid creative fatigue.

transcript.speaker: Maya Chen
transcript.text: Smart, one testimonial gets stale fast if it's the only thing anyone sees.

transcript.speaker: Nina Patel
transcript.text: Exactly the thinking there.

transcript.speaker: Jordan Blake
transcript.text: Okay, landing page, Maya you wanted to cover this.

transcript.speaker: Maya Chen
transcript.text: Yeah, so Derek reviewed the copy over the weekend, mainly flagging that we shouldn't headline with Snowflake integration since it's still in limited beta, not generally available yet.

transcript.speaker: Nina Patel
transcript.text: Good catch, we actually had that as the second bullet point on the page, I'll pull that down to a smaller mention lower on the page instead, maybe under a 'coming soon' framing.

transcript.speaker: Jordan Blake
transcript.text: That works, we don't want to promise something that's not fully shipped and then have sales fielding angry emails in three weeks.

transcript.speaker: Sam Whitfield
transcript.text: Appreciate that, nothing worse than closing someone on a feature that isn't actually ready.

transcript.speaker: Maya Chen
transcript.text: Otherwise the page looked good, the testimonial section up top is strong, and the CTA is clear. One small thing, can we add a case study link instead of just the pull quote, give people something to click into if they want more depth?

transcript.speaker: Nina Patel
transcript.text: Yeah, we actually have a full Northstar case study in the works, it's not quite done but I can get a draft version linked by launch, worst case I link the existing one-pager for now and swap it once the full case study's ready.

transcript.speaker: Maya Chen
transcript.text: That works, as long as there's something there.

transcript.speaker: Jordan Blake
transcript.text: Okay, let's talk webinars since that's a chunk of the budget. Nina, can you run through the topics and speakers?

transcript.speaker: Nina Patel
transcript.text: Three sessions, one every two weeks starting mid-October. First one is cohort analysis fundamentals, second is real time alerting and operational dashboards, and the third is a customer panel with Northstar and hopefully Fenwick if they agree to it.

transcript.speaker: Maya Chen
transcript.text: Who's presenting the second one, the alerting session? That feature isn't fully shipped either.

transcript.speaker: Jordan Blake
transcript.text: Good catch, that's actually why I wanted you in this meeting. I think we frame that session around the concept and early results rather than a full product demo, since alerting delivery won't be live until Sprint 43 at the earliest.

transcript.speaker: Maya Chen
transcript.text: That's safer, let's make sure whoever presents that one is clear it's a preview, not a general availability announcement.

transcript.speaker: Nina Patel
transcript.text: Noted, I'll build that framing into the talk track and run it by Derek before the session.

transcript.speaker: Jordan Blake
transcript.text: Speaker wise, I've got a draft list, mostly internal, Derek or someone from his team for the technical sessions, and I still need final sign off on that list.

transcript.speaker: Maya Chen
transcript.text: Right, I said I'd review that this weekend and get you a decision Friday morning, I'll stick to that.

transcript.speaker: Jordan Blake
transcript.text: Appreciate it, I want invites going out early next week so we're not scrambling for RSVPs.

transcript.speaker: Sam Whitfield
transcript.text: Quick question on the webinars, will sales get the registrant list in real time, or only after each session wraps?

transcript.speaker: Nina Patel
transcript.text: Real time, we're syncing registrations directly into the CRM as they come in, so your team can see who signs up as soon as they register, not just attendees after the fact.

transcript.speaker: Sam Whitfield
transcript.text: Perfect, that's actually a big improvement, last time we only got the list after the webinar and by then some of the urgency was gone.

transcript.speaker: Jordan Blake
transcript.text: Good, that was a direct fix based on feedback from you guys too.

transcript.speaker: Sam Whitfield
transcript.text: Appreciated. Let's talk about follow up SLA then, since that was my other concern from last time. What's the plan for how fast reps respond to a new lead from this campaign?

transcript.speaker: Jordan Blake
transcript.text: I want to propose a twenty four hour SLA for MQLs generated from paid social and the landing page, given how quickly interest can cool on outbound touches like these.

transcript.speaker: Sam Whitfield
transcript.text: Twenty four hours is doable, I'll make sure that's communicated to the team and we'll track it in our dashboard so it's visible, not just an informal goal nobody actually watches.

transcript.speaker: Jordan Blake
transcript.text: That would be great, can we also agree on lead routing, is it strictly by territory or do bigger accounts get routed to specific reps regardless of territory?

transcript.speaker: Sam Whitfield
transcript.text: Strictly territory for now to keep it simple, if something looks like a strategic account we can always reassign manually after the fact.

transcript.speaker: Jordan Blake
transcript.text: Works for me. Nina, are UTM parameters set up so we can actually attribute pipeline back to specific channels and even specific ad creative?

transcript.speaker: Nina Patel
transcript.text: Yes, every asset has a unique UTM, broken down by channel, campaign, and creative variant, so we'll be able to see exactly which newsletter or which ad version is actually driving pipeline, not just leads.

transcript.speaker: Jordan Blake
transcript.text: Good, that granularity matters a lot for how we allocate budget next quarter.

transcript.speaker: Maya Chen
transcript.text: Agreed, I'd love a mid-campaign readout in like three weeks so we can course correct spend if one channel's clearly underperforming.

transcript.speaker: Jordan Blake
transcript.text: Let's do that, I'll schedule a mid-campaign check in for the third week of October.

transcript.speaker: Nina Patel
transcript.text: I'll have the dashboard ready with live numbers by then, pulling from the CRM and ad platforms directly so we're not manually reconciling spreadsheets.

transcript.speaker: Jordan Blake
transcript.text: Perfect. Let's also quickly touch launch day logistics, anything blocking a clean October first launch?

transcript.speaker: Nina Patel
transcript.text: Only thing outstanding is the landing page edit we just discussed, everything else, ad creative, newsletter placements, webinar registration pages, is built and scheduled.

transcript.speaker: Jordan Blake
transcript.text: Great, I'll get that landing page edit prioritized today so there's buffer before launch.

transcript.speaker: Sam Whitfield
transcript.text: On my side, I'll get the SLA and routing rules documented and shared with the team by Monday so reps aren't caught off guard on day one.

transcript.speaker: Maya Chen
transcript.text: And I'll finalize the webinar speaker list by Friday like I said.

transcript.speaker: Jordan Blake
transcript.text: Great, let's recap. Nina handles the landing page edit today, drops Snowflake down to a coming soon mention, and gets the case study link or interim one-pager added.

transcript.speaker: Nina Patel
transcript.text: On it.

transcript.speaker: Jordan Blake
transcript.text: Maya finalizes the speaker list by Friday and I'll get invites out early next week once that's locked.

transcript.speaker: Maya Chen
transcript.text: Confirmed.

transcript.speaker: Jordan Blake
transcript.text: Sam documents the follow up SLA and routing rules by Monday, and I'm scheduling the mid-campaign readout for the third week of October.

transcript.speaker: Sam Whitfield
transcript.text: Sounds good, I'm on it.

transcript.speaker: Jordan Blake
transcript.text: Great, I think we're in good shape for October first. Thanks everyone, this was a productive one.

transcript.speaker: Maya Chen
transcript.text: Agreed, feeling good about this launch.

transcript.speaker: Sam Whitfield
transcript.text: Same, appreciate the tighter lead quality targeting this time around.

transcript.speaker: Nina Patel
transcript.text: Thanks all, I'll get moving on the landing page fix right after this.

transcript.speaker: Jordan Blake
transcript.text: Great, talk soon everyone.

summary.overview: Jordan led a final readiness review for the Q4 'Data Driven Or Die' campaign ahead of its October 1st launch, with Nina covering budget allocation, creative testing, and webinar planning, Maya relaying landing page feedback, and Sam representing sales' interest in lead quality and follow-up speed. The team confirmed the testimonial-led creative won A/B testing decisively and refined MQL targeting to director-level buyers at 200+ employee companies based on last quarter's lessons. Sales and marketing aligned on a 24-hour follow-up SLA, territory-based lead routing, and real-time UTM attribution. The only remaining blocker before launch is a landing page edit to soften Snowflake integration claims.
bullet_points: 💰 $45K Q4 budget: $20K paid social, $15K newsletters, $10K webinar series
🎯 MQL criteria tightened to director+ at 200+ employee companies
📊 Testimonial-led creative nearly doubled CTR (2.1% vs 1.1%) over feature-led messaging
🖥️ Landing page fix needed: soften Snowflake claims to 'coming soon', add case study link
🎙️ Three-part webinar series starting mid-October; alerting session framed as preview, not GA
⏱️ 24-hour lead follow-up SLA agreed with sales, territory-based routing
🔗 UTM tracking set up per channel/creative for pipeline attribution
📅 Mid-campaign readout scheduled for third week of October
